ground.silhouette: tiny fleshy rosette with white-pink flowers

growth.juvenile_note: Seedlings appear after snowmelt on scree and moraine: two small cotyledons, then a few fleshy, glossy, dark green leaves divided into three lobes. It grows very slowly in the short summers, building a small tuft of thick, deeply 3-parted leaves on a stout rootstock; flower buds take 2-3 seasons to develop before the first white flowers (ageing pink-red) open.
growth.source: German Wikipedia Gletscher-Hahnenfuss (5-20 cm; flowers 3 cm, white turning pink to dark red; blooms Jul-Aug; needs 2-3 growing seasons to form flowers; fly-pollinated; 2,300-4,275 m, highest flowering plant of the Alps); English Wikipedia (flowers 1.8-3.8 cm); ages estimated

ground.name: Snow algae
ground.source: Chlamydomonas nivalis (watermelon snow), cosmopolitan snowfield/glacier alga; pink surface film on summer snow (alpine and polar snow-algae literature)

traits.native_range: Chlamydomonas nivalis (watermelon snow), cosmopolitan snowfield/glacier alga
traits.note: leaf/trunk/petiole derived from the plant's shape class; per-species detail where the entry carries it (aroids, cannabis)

growth.juvenile_note: Nothing plant-like to see: overwintering red cysts in the snow and soil wake at snowmelt, release tiny green swimming cells (5-15 um) that move up through wet snow, then turn orange and finally into red resting cysts (35-40 um). What shows is a pink-to-blood-red 'watermelon snow' stain in footprints and sun cups that deepens over the summer.
growth.source: Wikipedia Chlamydomonas nivalis (green motile cells 5-15 um in spring-summer meltwater, orange stage, red cysts 35-40 um are the longest phase, cysts in the top 0-20 cm of snow, growth optimum 5-15C); bloom timing after melt onset estimated
